title: When something breaks
content:
## What you'll get

When your app errors or displays incorrectly, you can fix it with a single message - and you'll never lose progress thanks to automatic snapshots.

## If you see an error message

<Steps>
<Step title="Copy the entire error">
When something breaks, grab the **full error text** from your browser console or the error modal - including stack traces, file paths, and line numbers. Paste it straight into the chat with a short note:

```
please solve this error

[paste the complete error here]
```

The agent will read the stack trace, find the broken component or API call, and push a fix.
</Step>

<Step title="Add a screenshot for visual bugs">
If the problem is visual - a button hidden off-screen, wrong colors, misaligned text - upload a screenshot (drag and drop into the chat) and describe what you expected to see:

```
This modal is cut off on mobile (see screenshot). The submit button is below the fold.
```

The agent will adjust the layout or styles to match your intent.
</Step>

<Step title="Describe when it happens">
For bugs that come and go, share the context:

- **When** - "only after I log in" or "on the second page load"
- **Where** - which page or feature
- **What action** - the button click or form that triggers it

Example:

```
The "Add to Cart" button doesn't respond after I navigate from the product list. It works if I reload the detail page directly.
```

This helps the agent trace state or routing issues.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip>
Right-click an error in your browser console and select "Copy" to capture the full output, including all stack frames.
</Tip>

## If something looks wrong

Nothing is permanently broken. Every time the agent stops, the platform saves a **snapshot** of your entire app - code, configuration, and deployment state. If a change breaks a feature or removes something you need, you can **roll back** to any earlier snapshot.

### When to roll back instead of asking for a fix

Use rollback when:

- The agent removed a working feature
- A refactor broke an API that was fine before
- You want to undo several changes at once

<Steps>
<Step title="Open History">
Click the **History** icon in the left sidebar. You'll see a timeline of snapshots.
</Step>

<Step title="Preview the snapshot">
Click an earlier snapshot to see what changed between that point and now - added, modified, or deleted files are highlighted.
</Step>

<Step title="Confirm rollback">
Click **Rollback to this version**. The platform restores everything from that snapshot and redeploys automatically. Your current state is saved as a new snapshot labeled "Before rollback," so you can roll forward again if you change your mind.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
Rollback reverts code, environment variables, dependencies, and configuration. It does **not** revert database data (your MongoDB records stay as-is). If a schema change is incompatible with your current data, you may need to clean up records manually.
</Note>

### Rollback vs asking the agent to fix it

**Ask the agent** when the issue is small and you can describe what went wrong.

**Roll back** when you're not sure what broke, or when multiple changes need undoing at once.

## If something looks wrong - needs review

This section (using screenshots as prompts, automated test results, internal test builds) needs product confirmation before publishing.
</Callout>

You now know how to fix errors with one message and how to roll back when needed. Next, you'll add user accounts and login.
